note: The World Inequality Database (WID.world, bulk download of 15 October 2026, read again in that of 30 October 2026), Dominican Republic, 2024: average net personal wealth (ahweal992j) and average post-tax national income (adiinc992j) per adult over 20, resources split equally within couples, in DOP of that year, for the bottom 20, 40, 60, 90 and 99 percent and the top 1 percent; each family's band is read from them. Read 2026-10-30. Read again 2026-11-03 from the bulk download of 30 October 2026 (its country files dated 30 October 2026): every row quoted here, its year and its currency label stood as before, and no later year was given. Until 2026-11-03 this note and its sources wrote the variable codes with their age and population parts swapped (ahwealj992 for ahweal992j and adiincj992 for adiinc992j), codes no file of the database holds (its README: type, concept, age group, population, as in sptinc992j), and called adiinc992j post-tax disposable income, which its metadata names post-tax national income ([Post-tax national income]=[Post-tax disposable income]+[Public spending]). The national accounts (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-03: each band's income scaled by households' disposable income over national income), read 2026-11-03: the latest households' account published for this country was in UNdata's National Accounts Official Country Data (the United Nations Statistics Division's), Table 4.6 and Table 4.1, series 1000, SNA 2008, for 2016: the net disposable income (B.6n) of households (S.14), 2,856,369,981,515 less 841,363,056 (2,855,528,618,459), over net national income (B.5n) 3,337,985,920,307 less 143,561,525,794 (3,194,424,394,513), in the table's currency (Dominican peso), about 0.894. A ratio stands only from 2019 on (the lead's ruling of 2026-11-03), so it wasn't held, and each band's income stayed the database's post-tax national income, public spending included. The national accounts, searched again on 2026-11-03 in the central bank's own accounts: the Banco Central de la República Dominicana's integrated economic accounts (cei_2007_2017.xlsx) ran to 2017, its 2018-reference series giving supply and use tables and GDP but no sector accounts. For 2017, the gross disposable income of households with the non-profit institutions serving them (its note 1/) was 3,086,001.29 over gross national income 3,581,039.02, in millions of pesos, about 0.862, gross over gross. Before 2019, so not held, and each band's income stayed the database's post-tax national income, public spending included.
